issues.description: The problem statement/UML specifies StockIngredient.price as int, but the template repository defines it as double (and the constructor/getter use double). This creates a structural mismatch with the required class diagram and with the reference solution, and may confuse students about the correct type and method signatures to implement.
issues.suggestedFix: Change the template's StockIngredient.price field, constructor parameter, and getPrice() return type from double to int to match the UML/spec and the solution.

issues.description: The problem statement requires adding getters for all private fields; however, the template Stock class includes a public setter setStockIngredients(...) which is not part of the UML and undermines encapsulation expectations (students may rely on it although tests/spec likely expect stock modifications through add/take/addToStockIngredients/emptyStock). This inconsistency can confuse students about the intended API surface of Stock.
issues.suggestedFix: Remove setStockIngredients(...) from the template (and solution) or explicitly mention in the problem statement that it exists only for local testing and is not part of the required design/API.

issues.description: The problem statement specifies StockIngredient.price as an int (and its constructor as StockIngredient(String, int, int)), but the template repository defines price as a double and uses a constructor StockIngredient(String, double, int) with getPrice() returning double. This mismatch makes it unclear for students whether prices are intended to be integer-based or floating-point and complicates mapping the UML/requirements to the starter code.
issues.suggestedFix: Align the template with the specification by changing StockIngredient.price to int, updating the constructor signature to (String, int, int), and adjusting getPrice() to return int.

issues.description: The problem statement requires SealSaloon.calculateTotalPrice(Meal) and acceptSupplyDelivery(String,int,int) to be static, but the UML diagram shows them as instance methods (no static marker), and the template’s Main uses instance-style calls (shop.calculateTotalPrice(...), shop.acceptSupplyDelivery(...)). This cross-artifact inconsistency forces students to guess whether to implement static or instance methods and how to call them.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the artifacts consistent: either (a) update the UML and template Main to call these methods statically (SealSaloon.calculateTotalPrice(...), SealSaloon.acceptSupplyDelivery(...)), or (b) if instance methods are intended, remove the 'must be static' requirement from the problem statement and change the solution accordingly.
